mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market health that reduces corporate hiring capacity and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a synchronized demand contraction that triggers equity sell-offs through reduced corporate revenue visibility over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a federal funds rate increase above 5.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity multiples, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or regime-specific Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) above its 12-month average signals robust household demand that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS exceeds 12-month average, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 110.0 indicates manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate capital expenditure and profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 110.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), a payroll growth surge above 200,000 jobs signals labor market overheating that triggers aggressive rate hikes, reducing equity valuations over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% signals strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings momentum, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through sustained profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.
